assessment.nobel_worthiness: Coupled proton and electron movement is the central physical mechanism of respiration, photosynthesis and fuel-forming catalysis. The theory of proton-coupled electron transfer plus the experimental thermochemical framework (bond dissociation free energies, concerted versus stepwise pathways) gives a quantitative, transferable language of chemistry and bioenergetics. This is a fundamental mechanism stated in physical terms.
assessment.attribution: Meyer pioneered the early PCET concept and molecular electrocatalysis, Mayer the concerted proton-electron transfer framework and thermochemistry, Hammes-Schiffer the multistate theory and computation. Nocera is credited too (artificial photosynthesis, PCET in proteins) but with three slots his contribution reads more as application and demonstration than founding concept. A fair trio exists but the ordering of priority between Meyer and Mayer deserves care in the reports.
assessment.maturity: Over three decades the concepts are confirmed independently in enzymes, molecular catalysts and materials. The interpretation is stable and widely used, so recognition would be timely rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as one discovery or a field built from separate theory, thermochemistry and catalysis strands.
Relative priority among Meyer, Mayer and Nocera is not settled by the supplied credit.
I am relying on my own knowledge of the history and have not verified details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing that electrons tunnel over long distances through folded proteins, with rates governed by distance and the intervening medium, established the physical basis of biological electron transfer. It underlies how respiratory and photosynthetic chains work and is among the clearest cases of quantitative physics explaining a biochemical process, using time-resolved kinetics on ruthenium-modified proteins.
assessment.attribution: Gray and Winkler led the modified-protein tunnelling experiments and the pathways picture. The wider field was shaped by earlier theory (Marcus, already recognized in 1992) and by work from others, for example Dutton on natural systems, who is not among the credited names. The credited pair is a clean and plausible allocation, although the omission of others is a priority question.
assessment.maturity: The distance dependence and tunnelling-pathway picture have been confirmed repeatedly across systems for decades, including in respiratory enzymes. This is mature and the interpretation is stable.
uncertainties: Marcus theory already carries the central theoretical Nobel recognition, so the incremental discovery must be argued.
Priority relative to contributions by non-credited researchers, which I cannot verify here.
Whether the protein-specific experiments are seen as a single decisive discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase is the enzyme behind biological nitrogen fixation, and its structure and mechanism are among the oldest open questions in bioinorganic chemistry. The crystal structures of the MoFe protein and FeMo cofactor, the identification of the central carbide, and mechanistic studies of electron and proton delivery with the Fe protein are of great importance, and recent cryo-EM work on turnover states makes the dynamics visible.
assessment.attribution: Rees (and earlier collaborators) delivered the structural foundation and Einsle the high-resolution cofactor with its interstitial carbon. Seefeldt and Dean developed the mechanistic and genetic understanding, and Ribbe the cofactor biosynthesis. Choosing three means leaving out important contributors, and a prize here would need the committee to settle whether it honours structure or mechanism.
assessment.maturity: The structural work is firmly confirmed, but the catalytic mechanism, including how N2 binds and where hydrides sit, is still being debated. Recognition of the structure would be timely, while the mechanism may be only partly mature.
uncertainties: The reaction mechanism of N2 reduction is not fully resolved.
Allocation between structural and mechanistic contributors is difficult under a three-person limit.
I cannot independently verify the full contribution record of each name.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Femtosecond serial crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers permits structure determination from microcrystals before radiation damage and makes time-resolved structural movies of enzymes and light-driven processes possible. It combines methods and mechanism and extends what spectroscopy and structure can show together, which I value highly.
assessment.attribution: The concept of diffraction before destruction (Hajdu and colleagues, Chapman) and the first serial crystallography of photosystem I (Chapman, Fromme and others) are central. Schlichting contributed major time-resolved and mechanistic applications. Credit is spread across the method idea, the demonstration and the instrumentation, so a three-person set is arguable.
assessment.maturity: The method is confirmed across many facilities and systems, but the most mechanistically decisive time-resolved results are still accumulating, so some of the chemistry impact may be premature.
uncertainties: Crystallographic artifacts and the interpretation of time-resolved XFEL data remain debated in some cases.
The credit is split between concept, demonstration and facility building.
Whether the chemistry impact is already large enough, as opposed to a methods achievement.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mass-spectrometric proteomics changed how the proteome is measured, enabling identification, quantification and mapping of modifications and interactions across whole cells. The impact on biochemistry is large and lasting, and it follows the 2002 recognition of ionization methods in a natural progression.
assessment.attribution: Mann (high-resolution, quantitative and deep proteomics), Aebersold (targeted and SRM/SWATH-style quantitative proteomics and systems biology) and Yates (shotgun and database searching, MudPIT) are the most defensible three. Hunt, Heck and Gygi also made decisive contributions, and a three-person limit leaves a hard credit question.
assessment.maturity: The field is highly mature, and techniques are in routine use worldwide. Recognition is timely or even somewhat late.
uncertainties: Which sub-contribution is regarded as decisive, since it is a broad technology rather than a single discovery.
Priority and omissions among Hunt, Heck and Gygi.
This is an analytical method rather than a mechanism, so it ranks below mechanistic candidates for me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Multidimensional heteronuclear solution NMR (triple-resonance, TROSY-based approaches, relaxation dispersion) brought structure and, crucially, dynamics of large biomolecules into reach, and it directly shows the motions that underlie function, such as invisible excited states in enzymes. This is a method that makes dynamic mechanisms visible.
assessment.attribution: Bax developed key triple-resonance and residual dipolar coupling methods, Kay the methyl-TROSY and relaxation-dispersion approaches, and Clore the structure-calculation and early multidimensional work. Wagner and Palmer have strong claims too, and Wüthrich already received the 2002 prize for the foundation. The three-laureate limit is binding.
assessment.maturity: Many decades of use give strong independent confirmation, and the methods are standard. Recognition would be timely, although Wüthrich's prize makes novelty a concern.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 prize for NMR structure determination in solution.
Priority between Bax, Kay, Clore, Wagner and Palmer.
Whether the committee wishes to honour methods over a specific discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape and funnel theory gave a physical explanation of how proteins fold quickly and reliably, and linked simulations and experiments. It is a conceptual framework in physical language that shaped biophysical chemistry, though the practical effect is less direct than that of a method.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic with Bryngelson developed the funnel picture, Dill the hydrophobic and lattice models and Fersht the experimental phi-value analysis. The credit is distributed between theory and experiment, and finding three decisive names is harder than for the single-method candidates.
assessment.maturity: The ideas are well accepted, but the framework is partly conceptual, and the practical successes in prediction came from other approaches, which could make its role in recognition debatable.
uncertainties: Whether the discovery is attributable to a few clear individuals.
Experimental versus theoretical emphasis in a trio.
Recent success in structure prediction may overshadow this line of work for some members.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Biomolecular condensation reframes cellular organization as phase behaviour of multivalent macromolecules, which is physical chemistry applied to cells. The concept has already redirected cell biology and biophysics, and the quantitative work (sticker-spacer models, in vitro reconstitution) gives it chemical substance.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne showed liquid-like P granules and nucleoli, and Rosen produced the quantitative multivalent-interaction and reconstitution work. Pappu and Mittag contributed physical and sequence-grammar understanding. A trio around Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen is plausible but contested, and a Chemistry prize may be hard to distinguish from Medicine or Physiology.
assessment.maturity: Replication is broad, but the physiological meaning of many condensates, and the standard of evidence for phase separation in cells, remain disputed, so I consider it less mature than other candidates.
uncertainties: The in vivo evidence standard for phase separation is still debated.
Allocation among five credible contributors.
Fit with the chemistry rather than biology prize.
